text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Employers' Asssociation warns against erosion of competitive edge in labour costs, calls for legally binding collective agreements, limits on sympathy strikes; calls made in memorandum sent to political parties.
- Government appoints director for pharmaceutical services.
- Chamber of Commerce, Federation of Industry to open joint office in Brussels.

- Dockyard should be model of worker participation system, says Workers' Participation Development Centre. Centre based at Malta University made suggestion in memorandum to political parties. Dockyard is run by council formed of workers having role of directors.
- Prime Minister Adami speaks on government's employment record at independence day anniversary celebrations.
